parsed_output.target_core_mechanism: Manual entry of pantry items with expiry dates, generation of meal suggestions based on that data, and collection of self-reported food-waste metrics for pre- and post-intervention analysis.
feasibility_notes: Manual data entry is low‑tech and readily implementable on any smartphone platform
Meal‑suggestion algorithms can be built using simple rule‑based matching to pantry contents and expiry dates
Self‑reported waste metrics are easy to capture but rely on user honesty and recall
Overall system is lightweight and does not require complex hardware or external services
reality_dependencies: Recruitment of a representative sample of small‑household cooks willing to use the app for the study duration
Baseline measurement of participants' typical cooking habits and food‑waste levels
Reliable self‑reporting mechanisms (e.g., daily logs or prompts) to capture waste before and after intervention
Stable internet connectivity only for optional data backup; core functions work offline
Ethical approval and informed consent for collecting behavioral data
claims_needing_evidence: Providing pantry‑based meal suggestions leads to a measurable change in cooking behavior
The intervention reduces the amount of food waste reported by participants
Self‑reported waste data correlate sufficiently with actual waste to serve as a valid outcome measure
The suggestion engine produces recipes that users find acceptable and feasible to prepare
potential_blockers: Low user compliance with manual entry of pantry items and expiry dates

Participant attrition over the study period
Bias introduced by participants' desire to appear more sustainable
Limited statistical power due to small sample size
